clips.title: The story
paras: WANTED: Jai'vhanel is an Alliance bounty posted by the Auberdine Village Council in Darkshore. The notice calls for the elimination of Jai'vhanel, a maddened black owl known as 'Swordfeather' that has begun ambushing travelers along the road near Auberdine. Adventurers must hunt the creature near the ruins of Ameth'Aran and bring proof of her death to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea.

A posted notice from the Auberdine Village Council alerts travelers along the coastal roads of Darkshore to a dangerous menace. A prominent local owl known as Jai'vhanel, nicknamed 'Swordfeather', has succumbed to a sudden madness. Rather than keeping to the dense wilderness, she has begun ambushing travelers and couriers journeying near Auberdine, transforming an ordinary woodland predator into a critical hazard for the settlement.

To secure the safety of the roadways, the council has placed an open bounty on Jai'vhanel's head. Slayers are directed to track the black-feathered raptor to her hunting grounds north of the ruins of Ameth'Aran, along the mountain base. Hunters must bring back one of her distinctive jet black feathers to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea in Auberdine to verify the kill and collect their reward.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: A reward is being offered for the death of the owl "Jai'vhanel" also known as "Swordfeather".
Unfortunately this owl has gone mad and has begun to attack travelers as they journey along the road near Auberdine.
Jai'vhanel was last seen north of the Ameth'Aran ruins near the mountain base. Bring back one of her jet black feathers as proof of her death.
Reward claims for this bounty should be claimed with Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea in Auberdine.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Greetings, adventurer - what may the Sentinels assist you with today? Perhaps you are here to inquire about the bounty on Jai'vhanel?

clips.title: Completion
paras: It is good to know that issue has been taken care of, but it saddens me that we could not find another way. Jai'vhanel had been somewhat of a guardian of this area for quite some time, and I am not sure what could have caused her descent into madness.
Regardless, thank you for your service today, adventurer. The roads to Auberdine are safe for travel once again.
